protocol: Opponent spell casts on YouTube 2.6 matches (runs/live/vid_<vid>.yolo.jsonl, 4 Hz, made by live_ppo/eval/video_frames.py). Each cast is labelled by viewing frames: (1) a blind 2 fps contact-sheet pass over the match and (2) a full-resolution check of EVERY spell track the detector built in the match, whether it emitted, merged or dropped it. t is the video second of the first 4 Hz frame in which the spell is visible. For every labelled cast this was also YOLO's first sighting, so 'first sighting - label' is 0 by construction; the latency that counts is emission - label. Bias: step (2) only shows casts YOLO saw at least once, and step (1) at sheet scale missed a real Barbarian Barrel, so a cast YOLO never fires on may be missing from these labels. Recall here is therefore an upper bound. 'ambiguous' casts are not scored either way. Classes are YOLO class names; they map to engine cards through opp_plays.card_for_class.

QD_1suWFNKo.notes: Opponent deck: Graveyard / Poison / Barbarian Barrel. Every Rage track in these matches is a false sprite (our placement circle, our 'Boule de feu' label, pink beams).

uVf1EUszTIM.notes: Opponent Goblin Barrel deck. Every barrel is seen flying from the opponent's king toward our towers. Single-hit Fireball explosions at 563.5 and 613.75 are fire-spirit / unit hits, not casts.

iVgmnDX-GPY.notes: Match 1: the static 'Giant Snowball' at 4.5 s is the video's Subscribe overlay. Match 2 (window opens at 584 so it includes the first Fireball at 585.0): the opponent Fireballs our right princess tower again and again; each one is confirmed by its HP falling 253 (4352 -> 4099 -> ... -> 2328). Zap at 839.25 = placement circles. Our own Fireballs fly from our king toward theirs, and our Logs roll away from us.
